transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-01-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Morgan Reed (CTO, Gateway Labs), Priya Shah (Head of FinOps), Daniel Cho (ML Platform eng)

Summary: Quick live walk through of Redwood Console per-route usage analytics, cost decomposition and routes chargeback. Questions on VPC and encryption, latency SLOs, pilot scope.

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alex with Redwood Inference, this is Samira our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:04] Morgan: Good, thanks. Excited — we wanted to see how you handle per-route cost breakdown. Our finance team has been asking for better chargeback.
[00:12] Priya: Yeah we get a monthly bill and its basically a blob, need to split by product lines.
[00:18] Samira (SE): Totally. Today i'm going to walk through the Console — we'll show the usage analytics, how routes map to cost buckets, and the per-route dashboards. We'll also go into batching and quantization suggestions since those materially affect cost.
[00:30] Daniel: Quick context — we run mixed traffic: chat assistant, summarization, and embeddings for search. Peak QPS is about 600 and average is ~120, typical sequence lengths vary widely.
[00:40] Alex: Great. Samira, can you share screen and open the "Paths" lens?
[00:45] Samira: Yep sharing now. Sorry screen is a bit laggy, you should see the Console top nav, then Usage -> Paths.
[01:05] Samira: Here we have a map of routes — each route is tagged by owner, product, and environment. On the right side you can see tokens, calls, median latency, and a cost column which is unitized to your billing currency. Note the cost is decomposed into infra (GPU minutes), token processing and overheads.
[01:35] Morgan: Wait that cost column — is infra billed per-second? How does that translate to our invoice?
[01:40] Samira: Good q. Infra is attributed based on peak allocation and actual usage via sample windows. We convert GPU minutes into a per-call amortized cost and then apply sampling to reduce noise. Final invoice matches the usage objects we export to billing exports.
[02:02] Priya: How accurate is attribution for bursty calls? We have a lot of short spikes.
[02:10] Samira: For bursty traffic we recommend prefix caching and dynamic batching; Console flags routes with high variance and recommends warm pools or reserve bursts. Also you can configure a route to pin to dedicated capacity to avoid cross-route tail latency.
[02:35] Alex: We pulled a sample of your traffic before the call and pre-generated a route cost sample — Samira can load that CSV so you see real numbers.
[02:43] Samira: Loading sample now... (brief pause)
[03:05] Samira: Ok CSV loaded — you can see Route / Owner / Tokens / Calls / Median latency / Cost. Notice Route 3 (search-embed) has high tokens per call so it's the biggest cost driver even though call volume is moderate.
[03:28] Daniel: That makes sense, embeddings are expensive. Could we set different quantization or downsample embeddings for lower priority routes?
[03:40] Samira: Yes. Optimizer provides per-route quantization profiles; Console will suggest q4_0 or int8 for embedding models where quality loss is acceptable, and also suggests caching for repeated queries.
[03:58] Morgan: Ok about security — we need SOC2, SSO, and customer-managed keys. Is that supported by Redwood Private?
[04:10] Alex: Yes, Private supports VPC and KMS/HSM integrations. For SOC2 we have the attestation and whitepaper — i'll share the security pack after this call.
[04:22] Priya: Can you confirm logs retention and audit trails so our auditors can see per-token access?
[04:28] Samira: Audit logs are available; retention can be set per-contract. We can also limit token retention for sensitive routes.
[04:40] Morgan: Performance — for our latency SLOs we aim for <300ms p95 for assistant. How will console help us detect regressions?
[04:52] Samira: Console has latency lenses by route and model; you can set alerts on p50/p95 and tie them to rollouts. Also Optimize suggests batching/seq length improvements and shows token-level cost impact.
[05:10] Priya: For chargeback, can we export a daily CSV by route for ingest into our billing system?
[05:16] Samira: Yes, daily exports and an API endpoint. We also have a breakdown that maps to G/L codes if you provide the mapping.
[05:30] Daniel: Any support for tagging dynamic user cohorts? Some routes change owner depending on A/B tests.
[05:38] Samira: You can set multiple tags and time-ranged ownership; exports include tags with timestamp so you can retroactively recalc costs.
[05:50] Alex: Let's demo a couple of features — first the 'what-if' slider for cost vs latency.
[05:56] Samira: Right — open the Cost Optimizer. Here's a slider that simulates different batch sizes and quantization. If we increase batch size to 16 we see token cost drop by 27% but p95 increases from 210ms to 350ms for this route.
[06:20] Priya: Those numbers are helpful. Is that simulation based on real kernels or theoretical model?
[06:25] Samira: Based on calibrated kernel profiles from our runtime; we run microbenchmarks and then apply your sequence length distribution to predict impact.
[06:40] Morgan: About pilot — we'd want to try a narrow pilot with three routes: assistant, summarizer, embed-search. What success metrics should we set?
[06:50] Alex: Good framing. Typical pilot success metrics: 1) visibility — daily per-route cost reports, 2) cost delta — expected 15–25% reduction with recommended optimizations, 3) latency SLOs maintained or bounded increase, 4) integration of exports into your billing system.
[07:14] Priya: Timeline — we have an internal procurement window in mid-Feb. Could we aim for pilot to start second week of Feb?
[07:22] Alex: Yes that aligns. We'll send a scoped SOW and pilot pricing and security docs this week.
[07:30] crosstalk
[07:32] Daniel: Quick technical — can we run benchmarks in our VPC or do you run them in Redwood env?
[07:38] Samira: Both. For highest fidelity we recommend running the bench in your VPC with Private or Dedicated. We can also run synthetic runs in hosted to give a baseline.
[07:52] Morgan: Curious about fallbacks — if a dedicated pool is saturated will requests failover to hosted?
[07:58] Alex: Yes, routing policies can be set: strict dedicated-only or allow fallbacks. You can also set canary policies and automatic rollback if p95 exceeds threshold.
[08:12] Priya: Any mention of competitors? We've looked at Anthropic and a replicate-based hosting — whats the differentiator here?
[08:20] Alex: Biggest differentiators we pointed out are per-route economics and optimized runtime for inference, plus unified tooling across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. We also provide stronger observability for chargeback.
[08:35] Samira: And the optimizer suggestions — our console ties optimizations directly to cost delta which usually resonantes with FinOps teams.
[08:50] Morgan: Ok, good. Can you share a sample of the audit log format so our security team can sign off?
[08:56] Alex: I'll attach the security pack — it includes log schema and retention options.
[09:05] Samira: Scrolling back to the route table, notice the 'anomaly' flag — that's from our usage baselines. If a route deviates significantly you'll see both token anomalies and cost spikes.
[09:20] Daniel: How granular is the anomaly detection — can we tune sensitivity per route?
[09:25] Samira: Yes, sensitivity and detection window are configurable per-route.
[09:30] Priya: Ok final question — billing cadence and export frequency for chargeback?
[09:36] Alex: Billing is monthly by default but exports are daily; for pilots we do weekly reconcilations with customers.
[09:44] Morgan: Great. Thanks for the demo, this was useful.
[09:48] Alex: Next steps — I'll send the pilot SOW, security docs, and a sample CSV. Samira will share the dashboard link and sample export. We agreed target start second week of Feb.

Action items recap:
- Alex: Send pilot pricing + security pack by EOW (2026-01-30)
- Samira: Share dashboard shortlink and per-route CSV sample by 2026-01-27
- Morgan: Provide traffic mix and QPS by 2026-02-05

End of transcript
